# Packet diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-packet/grammar/packet.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Packet diagram syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `packet` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed packet with Langium (`packet.langium` and `common.langium` in
`@mermaid-js/parser`); the rules below are its token rules, in its order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive.

Each field and statement ends at a line break (or the end of the text); `;` is not a
separator. A field's bits are checked after parsing: each field starts right after the one
before it (the first at bit 0), a range does not end below its start, and `+0` is not a width.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A diagram is `packet` (or `packet-beta`), then fields and statements, one per line. The
`YAML`, `DIRECTIVE` and `COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are skipped before parsing.

```ebnf
packet = { NEWLINE } Header { NEWLINE | statement NEWLINE } [ statement ] EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = PACKET
               | PACKET_BETA ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Field
          | Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr ;
```

`0-15: "Source Port"`, `16: "Flag"` or `+8: "Data"`: a field, its bits (first and last,
one, or a width after the field before it) and its label. A field longer than a row is split
at each row end.

```ebnf
Field @Field = ( INT [ DASH INT ] | PLUS INT ) COLON STRING ;
```

`title TCP header`: the title drawn below the rows (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | PACKET_BETA | `packet-beta` |  | `packet-beta`: starts a packet diagram (the older name of `packet`). |
| INITIAL | PACKET | `packet(?:(?=%%)\|(?!\S))` |  | `packet`: starts a packet diagram. |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. mermaid@12 tries it as the longer alternative of `-`, so it is listed first. |
| INITIAL | DASH | `-` |  | `-` between the first and the last bit of a field, as in `0-15`. |
| INITIAL | PLUS | `\+` |  | `+` before a field's width in bits, as in `+16`: the field starts after the one before it. |
| INITIAL | COLON | `:` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the diagram. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the title drawn below the rows, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | INT | `0\|[1-9][0-9]*(?!\.)` |  | A bit number or a width: `0`, or digits without a leading zero, not followed by `.`. |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'` |  | A field's label: `"…"` or `'…'`; `\` escapes the next character, and a label may span lines. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\r?\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t ]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `[\t ]*%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `[\t ]*%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
